title: HybriScan: A Hybrid Scanning Framework for Real-Time Anomaly Detection in Heterogeneous IoT Networks
abstract: The proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) devices across critical infrastructure has introduced significant challenges in maintaining network integrity and detecting malicious activity at scale. Traditional signature-based intrusion detection systems exhibit fundamental limitations when deployed against polymorphic threats in heterogeneous IoT environments. This paper presents HybriScan, a novel hybrid scanning framework that integrates passive traffic fingerprinting with active behavioral profiling to achieve real-time anomaly detection across heterogeneous IoT networks. Our architecture combines a lightweight convolutional neural network (CNN) for protocol-agnostic feature extraction with a graph-based anomaly scoring module that captures inter-device communication patterns. We evaluate HybriScan on three publicly available IoT traffic datasets — N-BaIoT, MQTTset, and Bot-IoT — achieving detection accuracies of 98.7%, 97.2%, and 96.4% respectively, with an average inference latency of 14.3 milliseconds per packet stream. Comparative analysis against six baseline methods demonstrates that HybriScan reduces false positive rates by 31.4% while maintaining computational overhead below 12% CPU utilization on embedded ARM Cortex-A72 processors. The framework is designed for edge deployment and requires no cloud connectivity for inference, addressing privacy constraints in industrial IoT settings. Source code and pre-trained models are made available under an open-source license.

title: FraudShield: Privacy-Preserving Financial Fraud Detection via Federated Learning and Explainable AI
abstract: Financial fraud detection systems face a fundamental tension between predictive accuracy and data privacy: training highly accurate models requires access to sensitive transaction data distributed across competing financial institutions, yet regulatory constraints and competitive pressures preclude centralized data aggregation. This paper introduces FraudShield, a privacy-preserving fraud detection system that employs federated learning (FL) with differential privacy guarantees to enable collaborative model training without raw data exchange. FraudShield integrates a novel gradient compression scheme that reduces communication overhead by 67.3% relative to conventional FedAvg, and incorporates SHAP-based explainability modules that produce regulatorily compliant fraud justifications meeting GDPR Article 22 requirements. We conduct extensive evaluation on a real-world synthetic dataset comprising 6.3 million transactions spanning 12 months, simulating participation from five heterogeneous financial institutions with non-IID data distributions. FraudShield achieves an F1-score of 0.934 and AUC-ROC of 0.978, outperforming centralized baselines by 2.1% F1 while providing (ε=0.5, δ=10⁻⁵)-differential privacy. Ablation studies demonstrate that gradient compression does not degrade model performance beyond 0.3% F1 under aggressive compression ratios. The system is designed for integration with existing anti-money laundering (AML) pipelines and supports real-time inference at sub-50ms latency.

title: A Systematic Review of Chain-of-Thought Reasoning Techniques in Large Language Models
abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting has emerged as a foundational technique for eliciting multi-step reasoning capabilities from large language models (LLMs), enabling significant performance gains on complex arithmetic, commonsense, and symbolic reasoning tasks. This systematic review synthesises 74 peer-reviewed studies published between 2020 and 2024 examining CoT variants, their empirical outcomes, theoretical underpinnings, and failure modes. We categorise CoT techniques into four principal paradigms: zero-shot CoT, few-shot CoT, self-consistency CoT, and tree-of-thought extensions. Our analysis reveals that CoT improvements are most pronounced in models exceeding 60 billion parameters, suggesting an emergent threshold below which sequential reasoning steps provide negligible benefit. We further identify systematic failure modes including reasoning chain hallucination, step-level error propagation, and sensitivity to prompt template phrasing. This review contributes a unified evaluation taxonomy and highlights critical open problems including faithful reasoning verification, efficient CoT distillation, and cross-lingual generalisation. Recommendations for practitioners and future research directions are provided.

title: Practical Topological Quantum Error Correction on Near-Term Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum Devices
abstract: Quantum error correction (QEC) is widely regarded as an essential prerequisite for fault-tolerant quantum computing, yet its practical implementation on noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices remains constrained by qubit overhead and gate fidelity requirements. This technical article examines the current state-of-the-art in topological quantum error correction codes — specifically surface codes and color codes — and evaluates their feasibility for near-term hardware characterized by two-qubit gate error rates of 0.1%–1%. We derive analytic threshold conditions for the depolarizing noise model and present simulation results obtained using Stim and PyMatching over device sizes ranging from distance-3 to distance-11 surface codes. Our analysis demonstrates that current superconducting qubit platforms operating at 0.3% two-qubit error rates can sustain logical error rate suppression of approximately 10× per code distance increment, but require a minimum of 49 physical qubits for a single logical qubit with meaningful error suppression. We discuss architectural implications for hybrid classical–quantum error decoding pipelines and identify the syndrome decoding latency as the primary bottleneck in real-time QEC implementations.

title: De Novo Protein Structure Prediction Using Equivariant Graph Neural Networks with Torsion Angle Parameterisation
shortTitle: GNN-Based De Novo Protein Structure Prediction
abstract: Accurate de novo protein structure prediction remains a central challenge in computational biology, with implications for drug discovery, enzyme engineering, and fundamental understanding of molecular function. While AlphaFold2 has achieved remarkable accuracy for proteins with known homologs, its performance degrades for orphan proteins lacking detectable sequence homology in existing databases. This paper presents an equivariant graph neural network (EGNN) architecture that parameterises protein backbone geometry through torsion angles rather than Cartesian coordinates, improving physical validity of predicted structures and reducing constraint violation rates by 44% compared to coordinate-based baselines. Our model, trained on the CATH 4.3 non-redundant dataset, achieves median TM-scores of 0.82 on CASP14 targets and 0.74 on orphan proteins from the PSIPRED benchmark. We demonstrate that torsion-angle parameterisation confers implicit geometric constraints that eliminate the need for post-hoc structure refinement steps in 78% of test cases, substantially reducing inference time. Attention weight analysis reveals the network learns chemically interpretable features corresponding to secondary structure propensities and hydrophobic core formation patterns.
